title: Combed slip decoration on greenware
subtitle: Trailing and combing coloured slip on leather-hard greenware for feathered patterns
excerpt: Combed slip decoration is a traditional folk-pottery technique. Parallel lines of contrasting slip are trailed across a base slip coat on leather-hard greenware, then a comb or stylus is dragged across the lines to create feather or chevron patterns. The result fires to a crisp, colourful surface under a clear glaze.
sourceNotes: Combed slip technique widely documented in folk-pottery literature including Slipware references.

content.text: Metallic oxide slip colourants must be handled in dry form with a dust mask. Wear gloves and wash hands after working with iron, cobalt, or manganese oxide. Apply slips in a ventilated area. Kiln fire with ventilation.
Combed slip works well on flat dishes, plates, and shallow forms where the combing can be done in one confident pass. The

materials.name: Leather-hard earthenware greenware dish or plate
Metal or bamboo comb (5 to 8 tines, 10 mm apart)

content.text: Applying the base slip coat

Apply a full even coat of white slip to the dish interior using the mop brush. Work quickly in overlapping strokes, keeping the dish flat. The slip coat should be about 2 mm thick. Do not go over it a second time or the base slip will pull away from the leather-hard clay.
Allow the base slip to set for 3 to 4 minutes: it should lose its wet sheen but still be soft.
Trailing the contrast lines

Fill the squeeze bottle with the contrasting slip. Trail parallel lines across the dish at 15 to 20 mm intervals, working from one side to the other in one continuous motion per line. Keep lines as straight as possible.
Combing

Immediately while the trailing slip is still wet, draw the comb across the lines at 90 degrees from one end of the dish to the other in a single smooth pass. The comb tines will pull the contrast lines into a feather pattern.
For a chevron pattern: comb in alternating directions, first left-to-right, then right-to-left in the next pass, working across the dish.
Do not re-comb the same area. One confident pass gives the sharpest pattern; going back blurs it.
Glazing and firing

Allow to dry fully. Bisque fire. Apply a thin transparent earthenware glaze by dipping or pouring. Fire to cone 04 to cone 02. The slipped surface will fire crisp and the pattern will be preserved under the clear glaze.
Troubleshooter

items.problem: Base slip peels away from the clay in flakes after drying
items.cause: The base slip was applied to clay that was drier than leather-hard, preventing adhesion
items.fix: Work only on leather-hard clay. If the piece is too dry, re-wrap in a damp cloth for 30 minutes before slip application

items.problem: Combing pattern blurs into a smudge rather than crisp feathers
items.cause: Too much time passed between trailing and combing; or the trailing slip lines were too thin
items.fix: Trail and comb within 60 seconds. If the slip is already setting too fast, lightly mist the base slip surface with water from a spray bottle before trailing to extend the wet working time
